record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: Is there an identifiable onset of the strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma as a function of collision time, beam energy, volume, system size, or energy density, and how does collectivity and macroscopic behavior emerge as those conditions are varied?

evidence.quote: In the dash to new machines and higher energy, the question of the onset - exactly when (in time) and where (in energy or volume) we first produced the QGP - has been left behind, unanswered.

For the time being, there are many hints, but no conclusive picture. It may yet turn out that there is actually no clearly identifiable onset, that the transition is continuous and gradual in terms of volume (starting with pp) or energy density, and possibly even happens at different places for different observables.
Is there an onset of the sQGP, and how does collectivity and macroscopic behaviour emerge with system size and/or energy density?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic nuclear collisions, the strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma (sQGP) is a deconfined state of QCD matter believed to be produced when sufficiently high energy densities and temperatures are reached. Collective behavior in such collisions is typically diagnosed via observables such as anisotropic flow coefficients v_n, strangeness enhancement, jet quenching, and hydrodynamic-like azimuthal correlations, measured across systems ranging from proton–proton (pp), proton–nucleus (pA), to nucleus–nucleus (AA) collisions, and across a range of center-of-mass energies √s_NN, system volumes, charged-particle multiplicities, and inferred energy densities.

Determine whether there exists an identifiable onset of the sQGP as a function of (i) collision evolution time, (ii) beam energy √s_NN, (iii) interaction volume, (iv) system size (e.g., pp, pA, light-ion, heavy-ion), or (v) energy density. Specifically:

1. Establish whether collective and macroscopic (hydrodynamic-like) behavior appears at a sharp threshold in any of these variables, or instead emerges as a continuous and gradual crossover.
2. Characterize how collectivity—measured through flow harmonics v_n, their multiparticle cumulants, strangeness enhancement, and energy-loss observables—develops as the above control variables are varied, including in small systems (high-multiplicity pp and pA collisions).
3. Determine whether the onset, if any, occurs at the same value of the control variable for all such observables, or whether different observables turn on at different thresholds.

Provide either a quantitative criterion (with values of √s_NN, multiplicity, volume, or energy density) marking the onset of sQGP formation that is consistent with all relevant observables, or a demonstration that no such common threshold exists and that the transition to sQGP-like behavior is continuous.
artifact.status_search_result: The onset of the sQGP and the emergence of collectivity in small systems remain open questions in heavy-ion physics. Recent experimental and theoretical work (LHC, RHIC BES) continues to investigate flow-like signals in pp and pA collisions and the energy/system-size dependence of QGP signatures, without a consensus on a single identifiable onset; many results are consistent with a gradual emergence rather than a sharp threshold.

status_evidence.title: The Big Picture, and the Big Questions
status_evidence.snippet: There are many hints, but no conclusive picture... possibly even happens at different places for different observables.
status_evidence.claim: Onset of sQGP and emergence of collectivity remained an open question.

status_evidence.title: Collectivity in small collision systems (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews of small-system collectivity continue to debate whether QGP-like behavior emerges gradually with multiplicity in pp/pA, with no agreed onset.
status_evidence.claim: Question of onset/emergence of collectivity in small systems remains under active investigation.
